coverageMedicareAge.citation: Medicare eligibility at 65 (Social Security Act, Title XVIII); 95.1% of people 65 and over have it (Census ACS 2023).

coverageChildAge.citation: Medicaid and CHIP cover children through age 18; the Census coverage tables group people under 19 (ACS 2023, S2701).

coverageEmployeeShareSingle.citation: Average annual worker contribution for single coverage, 2023: $1,401 (KFF Employer Health Benefits Survey 2023, Summary of Findings), in minor units.

coverageEmployeeShareFamily.citation: Average annual worker contribution for family coverage, 2023: $6,575 (KFF Employer Health Benefits Survey 2023, Summary of Findings), in minor units.

coverageBenchmarkPremium.citation: The yearly benchmark (second-lowest-cost silver) marketplace premium for a 40-year-old with no subsidy, about $477 a month in 2024 (KFF, Marketplace Average Benchmark Premiums, 2024), in minor units.
coverageBenchmarkPremium.estimatedFrom: KFF 2024 national average benchmark; spread $400 to $600 a month by state

coverageNeedWeight.citation: How far age (the need for care rising from 19 to 64) pulls toward having coverage.

coverageCostWeight.citation: How far the yearly cost as a share of the household's income pulls against coverage.

coverageTemperamentWeight.citation: How far a person's temperament (every trait's lean toward taking cover over going without, from the shared trait table) moves the choice.

coverageEmployerStayPull.citation: The pull of declining an employer's plan, calibrated so take-up among eligible employees lands near 68.8% (AHRQ MEPS-IC 2023).

coverageMarketStayPull.citation: The pull of going without rather than buying a marketplace plan, calibrated so adults 19 to 64 are uninsured near 11.0% (Census ACS 2023, S2701).

coverageFullTimeHoursWeekly.citation: The ACA's full-time employee works 30 or more hours a week (26 U.S.C. 4980H(c)(4)); 91.9% of full-time employees in offering establishments are eligible against 21.3% of part-time (AHRQ MEPS-IC 2023).
